quest.title: A New Painting in Pale Scarlet
quest.rewards_formatted: Primogem x40, Mora x20000, Hero's Wit x2

chapter.num: True Tales of the Violet Garden: Act III
chapter.title: A New Painting in Pale Scarlet

dialogues.speaker: Kaedehara Kazuha
dialogues.text: #Greetings, {NICKNAME} and Paimon. I heard there would be guides for the Irodori Festival, but I didn't expect it would be you two.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Hehe, we didn't expect to see you either! Returning as a guest for the Irodori Festival, no doubt!

dialogues.speaker: Kaedehara Kazuha
dialogues.text: I was a little surprised myself when I received the invitation. But after wandering the outside world for so long, it is good to have an opportunity to return to my homeland and pay respects to my old friends.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Kazuha, when we saw you in the distance just now, you seemed to be looking for something. What happened?

dialogues.speaker: Kaedehara Kazuha
dialogues.text: Ah yes, you see, when I came off the boat with everyone just now, I suddenly heard light footsteps around me.

dialogues.speaker: Kaedehara Kazuha
dialogues.text: I could tell they were not footsteps of a regular passenger, but by the time I turned around, the person had already disappeared. I only heard a splash come from below the pier.

dialogues.speaker: Kaedehara Kazuha
dialogues.text: Even though I didn't manage to catch a glimpse of them, I found this strange piece of paper by my feet.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Oh, does the paper happen to have a poem written on it?

dialogues.speaker: Kaedehara Kazuha
dialogues.text: Huh, how did you know?

dialogues.speaker: Black Screen
dialogues.text: You tell Kazuha all that's happened over the last few days...

dialogues.speaker: Kaedehara Kazuha
dialogues.text: Fascinating. It's almost hard to believe such things could happen.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Kazuha, can you show us that piece of paper?

dialogues.speaker: Kaedehara Kazuha
dialogues.text: Sure, here it is. Please, have a look.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Last time, Aoi no Okina's poem ended with a reference to Akahito. And sure enough, this is a story about him.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: The story this time basically says that Akahito got his name from his love of red seals. However, the Shogun discovered that he had committed plagiarism, and he was soon exiled...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Well, if Paimon were to rate today's story, it sounds pretty unfortunate!

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Well, the other stories weren't much better either...

dialogues.speaker: Kaedehara Kazuha
dialogues.text: I don't think there's anything particularly wrong with this story. I, too, was once wanted as a criminal by the Shogunate, so I'm not all that different from Akahito mentioned in this story.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: But according to the story, Akahito was exiled by the shogun because of his wrongdoings. You did nothing wrong, Kazuha.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Huh? Traveler, what are you thinking about?

choices.text: The seal mentioned in the story...

response.speaker: Kaedehara Kazuha
response.text: Ah, by the way, you mentioned that your friend has been struggling because he's unable to sign his name quickly, right?

response.speaker: Kaedehara Kazuha
response.text: In Liyue and Inazuma, there is a saying: "that which has been stamped has also been signed." Perhaps using a seal could be a feasible solution.

response.speaker: Kaedehara Kazuha
response.text: While sailing at sea, I sometimes carve things to pass the time. If you wish to create a stamp for his seal, I might be able to help.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Wow, that's an idea! Quick, let's go tell Albedo.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Albedo, we've figured out a way to help Xingqiu!

dialogues.speaker: Black Screen
dialogues.text: You tell Albedo everything that happened with Kazuha...

dialogues.speaker: Albedo
dialogues.text: Interesting... A story of The Five Kasen appears again, and with a timely solution.

dialogues.speaker: Albedo
dialogues.text: A stamped seal, huh? Hmm, let me think.

dialogues.speaker: Albedo
dialogues.text: Indeed, it is an efficient solution. If we use a stamp, then Xingqiu won't have to struggle with his handwriting anymore. However...

response.speaker: Albedo
response.text: Since Xingqiu's signature has been previously revealed to the readers, it would seem insincere if he only used a stamped seal for his new books.

response.speaker: Albedo
response.text: But, I have another idea. Using a seal is a part of it, of course. Let's go to Uyuu Restaurant now to discuss my idea with everyone.

talks.objective: Look for Albedo at The Five Kasen Plaza

dialogues.speaker: Black Screen
dialogues.text: You carefully dip the paper into the water...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Wow, look! It's really working, more words have appeared on the paper!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Let Paimon see what it says!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Hmm, the story says that after Sumizome got the collection of poems from Akahito and put them into a stream of water...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: The plagiarized words in the poem became blurry... Huh, why would that happen?

dialogues.speaker: Kamisato Ayaka
dialogues.text: You see, Paimon, in the past, when printing was not yet well-developed, handwritten text could easily become smudged in books when exposed to moisture.

dialogues.speaker: Kamisato Ayaka
dialogues.text: To ensure the text lasted longer, they'd either write using a special ink or coat the paper's surface with a waterproof coating once the writing was finished.

dialogues.speaker: Kamisato Ayaka
dialogues.text: Such special inks are time-consuming and laborious to produce, and the waterproof coating could also prove just as difficult.

dialogues.speaker: Kamisato Ayaka
dialogues.text: However, since Akahito's poetry collection was an important gift to be presented to the Shogun, surely one of those two methods was used to protect it.

dialogues.speaker: Kamisato Ayaka
dialogues.text: But as for the plagiarized poems, not only would they lack Akahito's seal, but the words would also react differently when exposed to liquid.

choices.text: So this poem wasn't written by Akahito.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: *gasp* Which means Akahito didn't plagiarize his work! He was set up!

response.speaker: Albedo
response.text: Yes, it appears that this is the truth that Sumizome's story is trying to convey.

response.speaker: Albedo
response.text: Although the story is saddening, I've decided on the subjects to use for Akahito and Sumizome's portraits.

response.speaker: Albedo
response.text: Kazuha, Ayaka, would you be willing to be the models for my paintings?

response.speaker: Kamisato Ayaka
response.text: I would be delighted.

response.speaker: Kaedehara Kazuha
response.text: Yes, as would I.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: There you go! The next two portraits should be ready in no time!

response.speaker: Albedo
response.text: Yes, and now that all four stories have all been collected, the story of The Five Kasen is now fully completed.

choices.text: It was added later by someone else.

dialogues.speaker: Hirayama
dialogues.text: Yes, that's it, Zhenyu! Your writing has greatly improved today, which means yesterday's intensive training was effective!

dialogues.speaker: Xingqiu
dialogues.text: My apologies, but I simply can't do it anymore. My hands are so sore that I can't even move them anymore... *sigh* I should've known better than to read novels during calligraphy class.

dialogues.speaker: Hirayama
dialogues.text: You just had a ten-minute break. C'mon, you can do this!

dialogues.speaker: Onodera
dialogues.text: When it comes to pushing a deadline, there is no one more brutal than Mr. Hirayama.

dialogues.speaker: Murata
dialogues.text: No wonder Lady Yae would always send the editorial director to handle troublesome authors...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Whoa, this is getting scary! It hasn't even been that long and Xingqiu's already zombified.

dialogues.speaker: Albedo
dialogues.text: Mr. Hirayama, we found a solution that might just solve our dilemma.

dialogues.speaker: Albedo
dialogues.text: In both Liyue and Inazuma, seals are widely used as the equivalent of a signature. If we use a stamp to leave the author's seal on the books, then we could make the signature process a lot easier.

dialogues.speaker: Albedo
dialogues.text: Of course, a seal on its own is not enough. So, I propose that each signature consists of two parts.

dialogues.speaker: Albedo
dialogues.text: First, we'll use a personalized seal. We can simply carve one using Zhenyu's signature as the design.

dialogues.speaker: Albedo
dialogues.text: In addition, I'll also design a simple but elegant pattern that's easy for Zhenyu to write. That way, he will only need to draw a simple pattern on each book.

dialogues.speaker: Hirayama
dialogues.text: Hmm, let me think...

dialogues.speaker: Hirayama
dialogues.text: Alright, I think that would work! Not only does it still involve the author's own handwriting, but the result should be very beautiful as well.

dialogues.speaker: Xingqiu
dialogues.text: So what you mean to say is, I've been saved from this predicament?

dialogues.speaker: Onodera
dialogues.text: Mr. Hirayama, it suddenly occurred to me that the reason we gave up on live book signings previously was because it would take too long for the author to sign each book.

dialogues.speaker: Onodera
dialogues.text: But if we adopt Calx's proposed method, we might have enough time to do signatures at the live event.

dialogues.speaker: Onodera
dialogues.text: And if all the authors signed their books in the same fashion, then Zhenyu's signature wouldn't look out of place.

dialogues.speaker: Albedo
dialogues.text: If you think it's feasible, I would certainly be happy to design signatures for the other authors as well.

dialogues.speaker: Kaedehara Kazuha
dialogues.text: Yes, and you may leave carving the stamps to me.

dialogues.speaker: Hirayama
dialogues.text: In that case, I shall contact the other two authors participating in the new release event.

dialogues.speaker: Black Screen
dialogues.text: Shortly after, the two other authors arrive...

dialogues.speaker: Satomi
dialogues.text: It is a great honor to use a signature designed by Calx.

dialogues.speaker: Kadenokouji Kenzaburou
dialogues.text: My pen name is quite complicated and isn't suitable for signing events. However, if we implement this new format, then it'll be a dream come true for me as well.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Great! Looks like everyone's on board with the idea.

dialogues.speaker: Hirayama
dialogues.text: I'm sorry to have kept you busy for so long, Zhenyu. Please, take the next few days to have a good rest. We'll handle everything from here.

dialogues.speaker: Hirayama
dialogues.text: The books that Zhenyu already signed can be used as special prizes in future events held by the Yae Publishing House.

dialogues.speaker: Onodera
dialogues.text: Phew... we did it, the event is saved!

dialogues.speaker: Xingqiu
dialogues.text: Thanks to everyone's efforts, Onodera and I are finally free of that mess.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Hehe, that's right! You're finally free, Xingqiu. Maybe you should step outside for some fresh air.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Hey, Kazuha! Are you okay? You've been standing in front of this blank canvas for a while... and you don't look so good.

dialogues.speaker: Albedo
dialogues.text: Apologies for making a wild assumption, but has the story of The Five Kasen reminded you of anything?

dialogues.speaker: Kaedehara Kazuha
dialogues.text: Yes, a few things did come to mind, actually. However, they were nothing more than some past incidents regarding my family.

dialogues.speaker: Kaedehara Kazuha
dialogues.text: I don't mind sharing the stories, but I'd prefer not to bring you any more trouble.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Hey, we're all friends here, Kazuha. You can always tell us whatever's on your mind.

dialogues.speaker: Kamisato Ayaka
dialogues.text: Kaedehara, please forgive my assumption, but perhaps you are thinking of the Raiden Gokaden?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: The "Raiden Gokaden"? What's that?

dialogues.speaker: Kaedehara Kazuha
dialogues.text: It appears that Miss Kamisato and I were thinking of the same thing.

dialogues.speaker: Kaedehara Kazuha
dialogues.text: But it also has much to do with the Yashiro Commission. It would be improper to speak of it here without the consent of Miss Kamisato.

dialogues.speaker: Kamisato Ayaka
dialogues.text: It's fine. Those of us here are all trustworthy, so there isn't any harm in it.

dialogues.speaker: Kamisato Ayaka
dialogues.text: However, this matter is somewhat complicated and may be difficult to explain. Let me start with the Raiden Gokaden.

dialogues.speaker: Kamisato Ayaka
dialogues.text: As you all know, the Yashiro Commission's primary purpose is managing ceremonial and cultural affairs, and Inazuma's art of forging swords is a very important part of our culture.

dialogues.speaker: Kamisato Ayaka
dialogues.text: The Raiden Gokaden were once the top five schools of the forging art in Inazuma. Although these families were swordsmiths by craft, they also held many important positions in the Yashiro Commission.

dialogues.speaker: Kamisato Ayaka
dialogues.text: Unfortunately, of the five, only the Amenoma Art still maintains its artisan lineage. The descendants of the Isshin Art are also still alive, but the craft has been lost to time.

dialogues.speaker: Kamisato Ayaka
dialogues.text: The descendants of the Isshin Art are none other than the Kaedehara family.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Whoa! We knew Kazuha came from a noble family, but we had no idea about his connection to the Yashiro Commission and sword making.

dialogues.speaker: Kaedehara Kazuha
dialogues.text: Yes, but that's all part of the past now. The Isshin Art was lost with my great grandfather's generation.

dialogues.speaker: Kaedehara Kazuha
dialogues.text: My grandfather was dissatisfied with my great-grandfather's lack of effort. When he was young, my grandfather traveled all over Teyvat to find a way to revive the family business, but it was to no avail.

dialogues.speaker: Kaedehara Kazuha
dialogues.text: And in my generation, our last remaining family property was lost as well.

dialogues.speaker: Kamisato Ayaka
dialogues.text: I heard my elder brother mention that the decline of the Raiden Gokaden happened very rapidly. In a span of a few decades, three of the families suffered various misfortunes and disappeared completely.

dialogues.speaker: Kamisato Ayaka
dialogues.text: Later, there was speculation that all of these misfortunes stemmed from some background machinations, meaning that someone wanted to wipe out the Raiden Gokaden.

dialogues.speaker: Kamisato Ayaka
dialogues.text: However, since not every family of the Raiden Gokaden came to ruin, such explanations were treated as nothing more than a conspiracy theory.

dialogues.speaker: Kaedehara Kazuha
dialogues.text: Indeed, I've also believed such ideas were just theories and rumors.

dialogues.speaker: Kaedehara Kazuha
dialogues.text: However, I know that a major incident happened to my great-grandfather when he was young.

dialogues.speaker: Kaedehara Kazuha
dialogues.text: Not only did it affect the Kaedehara Clan, but it nearly jeopardized the Kamisato Clan's position in the Yashiro Commission as well.

dialogues.speaker: Kaedehara Kazuha
dialogues.text: After reading the story of The Five Kasen, I can't help but feel like it's pointing me toward the truth behind that incident.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: What exactly happened to your great-grandfather, Kazuha?

dialogues.speaker: Kaedehara Kazuha
dialogues.text: I still can't say, I need to speak with someone to verify the details. Let's meet here again at noon tomorrow.

dialogues.speaker: Kaedehara Kazuha
dialogues.text: I will tell you everything I know then.

talks.objective: Discuss further plans at the entrance to Uyuu Restaurant.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Hmm, we still have some time to burn, where should we go next?

dialogues.speaker: Kamisato Ayaka
dialogues.text: Traveler, there you are.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Oh, it's Ayaka and Venti... That's an interesting combo.

dialogues.speaker: Kamisato Ayaka
dialogues.text: I was just going to the festival venue to prepare the ikebana lesson, when I found a strange piece of paper on a flower stand.

dialogues.speaker: Kamisato Ayaka
dialogues.text: This bard just happened to be close by at the time. He informed me that you've also found similar papers recently. As such, we came together to find you two.

dialogues.speaker: Venti
dialogues.text: But the paper she found isn't quite the same as the ones we found before.

dialogues.speaker: Kamisato Ayaka
dialogues.text: Here's the paper. Please, have a look.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Huh, all the poems we found before were roughly the same length, but this one is only two lines!

dialogues.speaker: Albedo
dialogues.text: And even though there are only two short sentences, neither of them are next to the title or centered on the page.

dialogues.speaker: Albedo
dialogues.text: Hmm, the position of the writing seems to indicate that there is other content written on this paper besides these two lines.

dialogues.speaker: Xingqiu
dialogues.text: If we take the poem literally, it reads, "Dip this paper in water, and see the truth naturally appear."

dialogues.speaker: Xingqiu
dialogues.text: Speaking of which, I have an ancient text at home, specializing in ancient and exotic stories. It mentions a special ink that will show itself when wet, and disappear when it's dry.

dialogues.speaker: Venti
dialogues.text: So, shall we give it a whirl? It just so happens that there is a pond nearby.

talks.objective: Return to The Five Kasen Plaza at Ritou

dialogues.speaker: Black Screen
dialogues.text: Soon after, Albedo completes the two portraits...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Huh... *sigh*

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Yeah... Ever since we completed the story of The Five Kasen, there's still one thing Paimon hasn't been able to figure out.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: One of The Five Kasen is called Kuronushi, right?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: It's just that... How could the story of The Five Kasen finish without him appearing at all?

response.speaker: Venti
response.text: Oh, hahaha! Have you really not noticed?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Huh? Not noticed what? Ugh, this is no time to be playing games, Tone-Deaf Bard!

response.speaker: Albedo
response.text: What he means is that the story of Kuronushi was already embedded within the four poems.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Huh, really?

response.speaker: Venti
response.text: That's right. The key lies in the poem that Aoi no Okina wrote after seeing Sumizome rinsing the poetry collection.

response.speaker: Venti
response.text: An average person could never understand the scene of a young girl washing Akahito's poetry collection in a stream.

response.speaker: Venti
response.text: Even Aoi no Okina couldn't figure out the meaning behind Sumizome's actions. He was simply reminiscing and thinking about his old acquaintances.

response.speaker: Venti
response.text: However, for the perpetrator who framed Akahito, it was completely obvious.

response.speaker: Venti
response.text: He was worried that if this poem was seen by the Shogun, then the Shogun could discover the truth behind the plagiarism incident. If that happened, then he'd be finished.

response.speaker: Venti
response.text: So in desperation, he threatened Aoi no Okina to make him tear out this poem.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Which means... the one who threatened Aoi no Okina is the same person that framed Akahito!

response.speaker: Player
response.text: The culprit is none other than Kuronushi.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: What, Kuronushi!?

response.speaker: Venti
response.text: That's right. Though there are only four poems, they still manage to tell the complete story of all five kasen.

response.speaker: Venti
response.text: Since the Shogun mentioned in the poems is certainly not one of The Five Kasen, the only character left is the mysterious one with an unknown identity.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Ohh, okay... Paimon is finally starting to get it now.

response.speaker: Albedo
response.text: However, this also brings something else to mind.

response.speaker: Albedo
response.text: The story of The Five Kasen has more or less reflected everything that has been happening around us lately.

response.speaker: Albedo
response.text: Which begs the question... Is there a Kuronushi in our world as well?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: A Kuronushi... In our world?

response.speaker: Venti
response.text: Speaking of which, I wonder if our dear Kazuha has come up with anything.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Oh right, Kazuha! He's been pretty quiet this whole time. Let's ask him!

dialogues.speaker: Hirayama
dialogues.text: Onodera, please inform Lady Yae of the changes in the event planning when you have a moment. She will surely like to hear about our new idea.

dialogues.speaker: Hirayama
dialogues.text: You're a quick thinker, Onodera. As long as you exercise a little prudence, you'll be able to achieve great things in the future.

dialogues.speaker: Onodera
dialogues.text: Uh, got it. Thank you very much, Mr. Hirayama.

dialogues.speaker: Murata
dialogues.text: I suppose this is all a blessing in disguise, isn't it? I'm sure readers will be thrilled to hear that the release event will also have a book signing.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: It's already time for us to be at the docks. Let's go!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: The Arrival Schedule says: "Ship stopover, one person." Does that mean we're only welcoming one guest today?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Look, that figure on the wharf! It looks like Kazuha!
